title: Egg, whole, fried with animal fat or meat drippings

content.title: About
content.content: Eggs are a nutrient‑dense food produced by chickens. When fried in animal fat or meat drippings they acquire a distinctive flavor and a higher calorie count compared with cooking without added fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Frying eggs in animal fat is a traditional technique in many cuisines, including French, Spanish and American home cooking.
The type of fat used influences taste and texture: butter yields a softer egg, while lard creates a crispier edge.
Eggs cooked in animal fat retain most of their B‑vitamins and minerals, but they also contain more saturated fat.
In 1933 this method was common in households because lard and butter were readily available.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A large egg provides about 6 g of complete protein, essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: The yolk is one of the few natural food sources of vitamin D, important for bone health and immune function.

items.title: Contains choline
items.content: Choline supports liver function and brain health, aiding memory and concentration.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Eggs supply iron, zinc and selenium, which play roles in metabolism and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in the yolk help protect the eyes from age‑related degeneration.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Frying in animal fat adds saturated fat, which can raise cholesterol levels if consumed frequently.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Eggs fried in fat are more calorie‑dense, which should be considered in weight‑management plans.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked eggs may contain Salmonella; cook until the yolk is fully set to reduce risk.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Egg white protein is a common allergen, especially in children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried eggs are served hot, often seasoned with salt and pepper. They can be placed in sandwiches, salads, burgers, or enjoyed on their own as a classic breakfast.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw eggs in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C in their original carton. Cooked fried eggs should be eaten within 2 hours at room temperature or refrigerated and consumed within 24 hours.
